I found 13 methods in `tokio/src` that call `trace::async_op` directly. Every call site uses the `trace::async_op(` path, so I searched the source for that name and then matched each call to the method that contains it.

- **`tokio/src/sync/rwlock.rs`**: `RwLock.read`, `RwLock.read_owned`, `RwLock.write`, `RwLock.write_owned`
- **`tokio/src/sync/semaphore.rs`**: `Semaphore.acquire`, `Semaphore.acquire_many`, `Semaphore.acquire_owned`, `Semaphore.acquire_many_owned`
- **`tokio/src/sync/oneshot.rs`**: `Sender.closed`
- **`tokio/src/sync/mutex.rs`**: `Mutex.lock`, `Mutex.lock_owned`
- **`tokio/src/sync/barrier.rs`**: `Barrier.wait`
- **`tokio/src/time/interval.rs`**: `Interval.tick`

I left some places out on purpose. `oneshot.rs`, `time/sleep.rs` and `batch_semaphore.rs` create spans named `"runtime.resource.async_op"` with `tracing::trace_span!` rather than calling the function. The remaining matches are in the tracing-instrumentation tests.
